MOTION TO STRIKE COMPLAINT
Off Calendar Jul-28-2026 Continued To Sep-14-26 At 09:00 A.M. In Dept 302
MINI MINUTES:

No appearances. The Court adopts the tentative ruling as follows:

Defendant Home Depot U.S.A., Inc.'s Motion to Strike Complaint is CONTINUED TO SEPTEMBER 14, 2026, AND ALL PARTIES ARE ORDERED TO TAKE CERTAIN ACTIONS.

The instant motion is continued to September 14, 2026, at 9 a.m. in this department.

As the court previously noted, this action is provisionally complex. (See California Rules of Court, rule 3.400(c)(6) ["[A]n action is provisionally a complex case if it involves one or more of the following types of claims: (6) [e]nvironmental or toxic tort claims involving many parties."].) On 6/15/2026, the court ordered the parties forthwith to meet and confer regarding complex designation and pursue complex designation under California Rules of Court, rule 3.403(b) and San Francisco Local Rule, rule 3.5(C)(2)&(3). Moving Defendant, here, has filed a motion to designate case as complex and noticed it for hearing in this department. That is not the process set out in Local Rule, rule 3.5. The parties are ordered forthwith to file an application for complex designation with copies to Department 304. At least five court days before any hearing in this department, the parties must file a joint statement regarding the status of complex designation. The moving party or parties must deliver a courtesy copy of the joint statement to this department within 24 hours of lodging the statement for filing. A failure to follow these orders may result in the motion to strike being ordered off calendar.

The record before the court demonstrates Plaintiff has failed to meet and confer as ordered by the court on 6/15/2026. Continued failure to meet and confer may result in a finding of contempt or sanctions.

Moving Defendants are ordered to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and email it to contestdept302tr@sftc.org prior to the time set for hearing.

Order is signed.

Judge: Joseph M. Quinn, Clerk: M. Goodman, Not Reported. (302/JMQ)

DEFENDANT HOME DEPOT U.S.A., INC.'s MOTION TO STRIKE COMPLAINT.

Defendant Home Depot U.S.A., Inc.'s Motion to Strike Complaint is CONTINUED TO JULY 28, 2026, AND ALL PARTIES ARE ORDERED TO TAKE CERTAIN ACTIONS.

The instant motion is continued to July 28, 2026, at 9 a.m. in this department.

The parties are advised that this action is provisionally complex. (See California Rules of Court, rule 3.400(c)(6) ["[A]n action is provisionally a complex case if it involves one or more of the following types of claims: (6) [e]nvironmental or toxic tort claims involving many parties."].) This fact may have been overlooked at the time of filing, given Plaintiff filed an outdated version of the Civil Case Cover Sheet. In any event, the court orders the parties forthwith to meet and confer regarding complex designation and pursue complex designation under California Rules of Court, rule 3.403(b) and San Francisco Local Rule, rule 3.5(C)(2)&(3). If any matter is noticed for this department in the future, the parties must file a joint statement regarding the status of complex designation at the time the motion is filed. The parties are ordered to file such a joint statement five court days before the hearing or continued hearing on any pending demurrer or motion with a courtesy copy delivered to the department within 24 hours of lodging the statement for filing.

Moving Defendants are ordered to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and email it to contestdept302tr@sftc.org prior to the time set for hearing.

Order is signed.

Judge: Joseph M. Quinn, Clerk: M. Goodman, Not Reported. (302/JMQ)
